about.title: About
about.lead: Octava is a guitar songbook devoted to Balkan and regional music — chords written above the lyrics, the way the song is actually played.
about.why: The big international songbooks barely cover this repertoire. Sevdalinka, starogradska and ex-Yugoslav classics are mostly passed down by ear and scattered across forums in inconsistent form. Octava gives them one place, with the tools a guitarist actually uses while playing.
about.notation: We use the local system: {h} is the twelfth degree, and sharps are written instead of flats — so {sharp}, not {flat}. Imports understand American notation too, so songs from foreign sources map across correctly.
about.tunerDesc: {link} — hears the note through the microphone and shows how far off it is, in cents. The audio is processed in your browser and never sent anywhere.
about.transposeDesc: {name} — all twelve keys, and which capo position gets you the same sound without changing your shapes.
about.diagramsDesc: {link} — hover a chord and see where the fingers go.
about.scrollDesc: {name} — the page moves on its own while you play, at a speed you set.
about.content: Songs are entered and checked by editors. If one is missing you can {request} it — we work through them in order of votes.

privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.collect: Without an account we collect nothing that identifies you. If you create one, we store your {email}, {username} and {password} — the password is never kept in readable form and we cannot read it. The list of songs you save is attached to it.
privacy.cookies: We use one cookie, and only while you are signed in — it keeps your session. It is set {httpOnly}, which means scripts in the browser cannot reach it. {noTracking}
privacy.noTracking: We have no tracking cookies and no advertising.
privacy.browser: Text size and scroll speed are remembered locally, in your own browser. That data never reaches us and disappears when you clear the site’s data.
privacy.mic: The tuner asks for the microphone only while it is running. The audio is processed entirely in your browser — nothing is recorded, sent or stored.
privacy.rights: You can ask to see your data, to correct it, or to delete your account. Deleting the account removes the email, the username and the saved songs.
privacy.noContact: An address for data requests belongs here. Until there is one, a reader has no way to exercise any of the rights above.
privacy.disclaimer: This text describes how the site actually works, but it is not legal advice. Have someone qualified review it before launch.

terms.title: Terms of use
terms.intro: Octava is a guitar songbook. These terms describe what you can expect from us and what we expect from you. By using the site you accept them.
terms.account: You do not need an account to read. You need one to save songs, rate them and write reviews. One person, one account, with a working email address. Your password is your responsibility; if you think someone else knows it, change it.
terms.accountAge: If you are under 14, open an account with a parent’s permission.
terms.content: Reviews, comments and song requests are yours and stay yours. By posting them you give us the right to display them on the site, and nothing beyond that. You can remove them whenever you like.
terms.contentRules: Do not post: insults or hate speech, other people’s personal data, advertising, or complete song lyrics.
terms.contentModeration: Editors may hide content that breaks these rules. The reason is always recorded.
terms.copyrightLead: This is the most important section on this page, so it is written plainly.
terms.copyright: Songs belong to their authors, composers and publishers. Octava claims no rights over any song. What is here are chord charts — how someone plays a song — not the songs themselves.
terms.copyrightNotice: If you hold rights to something here and believe it should not be, tell us and we will take it down. We do not ask for proof first and we do not argue first — we remove it, then we talk.
terms.use: Read, play, share links. Do not harvest the catalogue automatically, mirror the site, or load it heavily enough to get in other people’s way.
terms.availability: The site runs as well as we can manage, but we do not promise it will always be available. Features may change or disappear. If it ever shuts down, we will do our best to say so in advance.
terms.liability: Chords are entered by editors and other people, and mistakes happen. You use the content at your own risk, and we are not liable for damage arising from that use.
terms.end: You can delete your account whenever you want. We may close it if these terms are broken badly or repeatedly — and we will tell you why.
terms.changes: These terms may change. The date at the top shows when they were last touched. If something significant changes, we will say so on the site.
terms.law: The law of Bosnia and Herzegovina applies.
terms.noContact: An address for rights-holder notices and account questions belongs here. Without one, the takedown promise in the copyright section means nothing — there is nobody to send it to.
terms.disclaimer: This text describes how the site actually works, but it is not legal advice. Have someone qualified review it before launch — the copyright section above all.

recognize.title: Recognise a song
recognize.lead: Play a song near your phone and Octava opens its chords.
recognize.hint: Ten seconds is enough. It recognises recordings — live playing it cannot.
recognize.unsureHint: Try closer to the speaker, or play a part where someone is singing.
recognize.noPermissionHint: Allow the microphone in your browser settings, then try again.
recognize.failedHint: The recording was interrupted. Try again.

recognize.emptyHint: Recognition searches a library of fingerprints, and it is empty for now. Nothing to do with your recording.
